subject: Data Engineering
title: Cleaning Dirty Data
description: A fast breakdown of Cleaning Dirty Data for builders.

hook.text: A customer name field contains 'N/A', '0', a phone number, and an emoji. Welcome to real data.

buildup.text: Data cleaning fixes nulls, trims whitespace, standardizes formats, and removes invalid entries.

discovery.text: The 80/20 rule hits hard: engineers spend 80% of their time cleaning and only 20% analyzing.

twist.text: You can never clean all the dirt. The goal is to catch enough to make downstream results trustworthy.

climax.text: Automated cleaning rules plus manual review of edge cases is the practical middle ground.

punchline.text: Clean enough beats perfect. Perfect never ships.

quiz.question: What is the '80/20 rule' often cited in data engineering?
options: 80% of time is spent cleaning data, 20% analyzing
80% of data is useful, 20% is noise
